review.body: Requesting changes before merge. I re-ran the relevant validation locally and found three issues that should be fixed before this lands: the committed PR state leaves the worker test suite broken after the CORS header revert, `hls.js` is being pulled into the main bundle for a rare fallback path, and the new `showByDefault` sync can override a moderator's manual toggle when reports finish loading.

comment.body: This fixes the initial flash/collapse race, but it also means any later `showByDefault` transition from `false` to `true` will overwrite a moderator's manual toggle. In `ReportDetail`, `showByDefault` now starts false while reports are loading and then flips to true when `hasHighPriorityReports === false`, so this effect will reopen media even if the user explicitly hid it. Please preserve explicit user intent here and only apply the async default without clobbering a manual toggle.

This eager import pulls `hls.js` into the main app bundle even though it is only used after native video playback fails. I built both revisions locally: `origin/main` produces a ~964 kB minified main chunk (~270 kB gzip), while this branch jumps to ~1491 kB (~433 kB gzip). That is a large regression for a rare fallback path. Please move this to a dynamic `import('hls.js')` inside the fallback branch so the cost is only paid when the fallback is actually needed.

This assertion became stale in the second commit. `fix: remove global CORS credentials` removed `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` from `buildCorsHeaders`, but these two expectations stayed behind, so `cd worker && npx vitest run` fails on the committed PR state. Please drop the leftover credential assertions here and in the matching preview-origin test below so the documented worker suite stays green.

issue.title: Age review: Zendesk integration for parent contact workflow
issue.body:
## Context

PR #67 adds the age review clock — 15-day case management for under-16 reports. When a flagged user submits their parent's email via the mobile app, the email is saved to the case and the clock pauses. Currently, the moderator sees the email in the admin UI and handles outreach manually.

This issue adds Zendesk automation so parent contact is tracked as a ticket with proper threading, SLA, and reply detection.

## Scope

### Outbound: auto-create Zendesk ticket on parent email submission

When `POST /v1/minor-review-cases/{caseId}/parent-contact` saves the parent email:

- Create a Zendesk ticket addressed to the parent email
- Template body explains the situation, asks parent to reply to verify
- Tag the ticket `age-review` + include case ID in a custom field or internal note
- Use existing Zendesk API patterns from `worker/src/index.ts` (ticket creation, custom fields)
- Non-blocking: ticket creation failure should not fail the parent-contact endpoint (log + continue)

### Inbound: webhook on parent reply

- New endpoint: `POST /api/zendesk/age-review-reply` (sits alongside existing `/api/zendesk/` routes, uses Zendesk webhook auth)
- Zendesk trigger: when a ticket tagged `age-review` receives a new reply from the requester, fire webhook
- Handler matches ticket to case (by case ID in custom field or by requester email lookup)
- Updates case: log that parent contact was received, optionally transition state to `submitted_for_review`
- Moderator still makes the final clear/deny decision

### Zendesk-side configuration

- New trigger: "Age review — parent replied" (condition: tag `age-review`, requester replied)
- Webhook target pointing at `POST /api/zendesk/age-review-reply` on the worker
- Custom field or tag convention for linking ticket to case ID
- Email template for outbound parent notification

## Dependencies

- PR #67 (age review clock) must be merged first
- `ZENDESK_API_TOKEN` and `ZENDESK_EMAIL` env vars (already available on the worker for existing Zendesk integration)

## Not in scope

- Auto-closing cases based on Zendesk ticket resolution (moderator decision stays manual)
- Parent identity verification beyond "they replied to the email"
- Multi-language email templates (English only for MVP)

issue.title: feat(auto-hide): configurable tiers, settings UI, media proxy fixes
issue.body:
## Summary

- **Auto-hide settings UI** — new `AutoHideSettings` component in the Settings tab for configuring auto-hide tiers (Immediate + Threshold), trusted clients, categories, and thresholds. Uses `getApiHeaders()` for CF Access auth.
- **ReportWatcher tier-aware auto-hide** — `processAutoHide` now reads tier config from DO storage, routes reports to immediate (single trusted-client report) or threshold (N unique reporters per category) processing paths. Threshold counting is category-scoped via exact `reason` match in D1.
- **Media proxy hardening** — fixes a dead-end state where proxy-fetched content that isn't renderable (e.g. non-video blob) caused a permanent black frame instead of falling back to the broken-media icon. Adds `key={displayUrl}` to force remount when proxy URL arrives.
- **QUARANTINE recognized as blocked** — `useMediaStatus` now treats `QUARANTINE` (moderation-service D1 action) as a blocked state, so the action bar correctly shows "Unblock Media" instead of "Block Media & Ban Event" for quarantined items.
- **Pending review filters** — auto-hide actions excluded from resolved targets so auto-hidden items appear in the pending review queue. Category filter cleared when toggling pending review on.
- **BLOSSOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET** binding added to prod and staging wrangler configs (Secrets Store).
- **Blob URL cleanup** on unmount for `InlineMediaPreview` (memory leak fix).

## What changed (by area)

### Worker (Durable Object)
- `ReportWatcher.ts`: tier-aware `processAutoHide`, category-scoped `countUniqueReporters`, config GET/PUT endpoints, `isAlreadyAutoHidden` deduplication
- `ReportWatcher.test.ts`: 163 tests covering immediate/threshold tiers, trusted client gating, config validation, deduplication
- `index.ts`: forward request body to DO for PUT /config

### Frontend
- `AutoHideSettings.tsx`: new settings UI with chip lists for categories/clients, tier config, client-side validation
- `MediaPreview.tsx`: proxy blob recovery, blob URL cleanup, `key={displayUrl}` remount
- `useMediaStatus.ts`: QUARANTINE recognized as blocked
- `Reports.tsx`: auto-hide actions excluded from resolved, category filter cleared on pending review toggle
- `SettingsDashboard.tsx`: mounts `AutoHideSettings`

### Config
- `wrangler.prod.toml`, `wrangler.staging.toml`: BLOSSOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET secrets store binding

## Test plan

- [x] Deploy to staging (test instance), verify auto-hide settings load and save
- [x] Trigger threshold-tier auto-hide with 2 reports from different pubkeys, same category — confirm event is hidden
- [x] Verify single cross-category report does NOT trigger threshold (category scoping)
- [x] Confirm CSAM/immediate tier fires on single trusted-client report
- [ ] Open a report with quarantined media — verify "Unblock Media" button appears (not "Block Media & Ban Event")
- [ ] Verify media proxy shows broken icon (not black frame) when proxy content is unrenderable
- [ ] Verify pending review toggle shows auto-hidden items, not resolved items

issue.title: Investigate and remove stale `worker/public` frontend artifacts if no active deployment path depends on them.
issue.body:
## Summary
`worker/public` appears to be stale checked-in frontend build output, while the active frontend deployment path is Cloudflare Pages from `dist`.

## Why this needs investigation
- The repo currently points frontend deployment at `dist` via Pages.
- Worker configs and runtime appear API-only.
- `worker/public` duplicates built frontend artifacts and creates review noise, but an undocumented external deploy step or manual workflow could still depend on it.

## Goal
Confirm whether any active deployment path, CI job, or operational process still depends on `worker/public`.

If nothing depends on it:
- remove `worker/public` from the repo
- remove any workflow that regenerates or updates it
- update docs so the frontend artifact and deployment path have a single source of truth

If something does depend on it:
- document that dependency explicitly
- explain why the artifact belongs in this repo
- make the ownership and generation path consistent with the rest of the deployment architecture

## Definition of done
There is one documented, authoritative frontend artifact path and `worker/public` is either removed or justified.

issue.body:
## Summary

Adds `blob:` to the `media-src` CSP directive in `index.html`. Proxied restricted media creates blob URLs that `media-src 'self' https:` was blocking. `img-src` and `connect-src` already allow `blob:` -- this aligns `media-src`.

Restricted video content loads through the admin media proxy (`/api/media-proxy/{sha256}`), which fetches from the media server's admin endpoint and creates a blob URL for the `<video>` element. CSP was blocking the blob URL, causing the AlertTriangle fallback instead of the video preview.

issue.title: feat(reports): add NS-prefixed CATEGORY_LABELS for mobile report reasons
issue.body:
## Problem

divine-mobile is adding NIP-32 l/L tags to Kind 1984 events to restore app-level report categorization (see divinevideo/divine-mobile#3488). The l tags use the format `NS-{reason.name}` (e.g., `NS-csam`, `NS-violence`, `NS-harassment`).

`getReportCategory()` already reads l tags as a fallback, but `CATEGORY_LABELS` only maps `NS-csam` and `NS-ai-generated`. The remaining 8 mobile reason names with NS- prefix are unmapped and would display as raw strings.

## Solution

Add 8 new entries to `CATEGORY_LABELS` in `src/lib/constants.ts`:

- `NS-spam` -> Spam
- `NS-harassment` -> Harassment
- `NS-violence` -> Violence
- `NS-sexualContent` -> Sexual Content
- `NS-copyright` -> Copyright
- `NS-falseInformation` -> Misinformation
- `NS-aiGenerated` -> AI Generated (note: camelCase, distinct from existing `NS-ai-generated` which is divine-web's kebab-case format)
- `NS-other` -> Other

## Related

issue.title: fix: add blob: to media-src CSP for proxied video previews
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds `blob:` to the `media-src` CSP directive in `index.html`. Proxied restricted media creates blob URLs that `media-src 'self' https:` was blocking. `img-src` and `connect-src` already allow `blob:` -- this aligns `media-src`.

## Motivation

Restricted video content loads through the admin media proxy (`/api/media-proxy/{sha256}`), which fetches from the media server's admin endpoint and creates a blob URL for the `<video>` element. CSP was blocking the blob URL, causing the AlertTriangle fallback instead of the video preview.

## Related Issue

- Relates to moderation media preview workflow

## Validation

- [x] `npm run test`
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npx vite build`
- [x] No worker code changed

issue.title: Investigate and remove stale `worker/public` frontend artifacts if no active deployment path depends on them.
issue.body:
## Summary
`worker/public` appears to be stale checked-in frontend build output, while the active frontend deployment path is Cloudflare Pages from `dist`.

## Why this needs investigation
- The repo currently points frontend deployment at `dist` via Pages.
- Worker configs and runtime appear API-only.
- `worker/public` duplicates built frontend artifacts and creates review noise, but an undocumented external deploy step or manual workflow could still depend on it.

## Goal
Confirm whether any active deployment path, CI job, or operational process still depends on `worker/public`.

If nothing depends on it:
- remove `worker/public` from the repo
- remove any workflow that regenerates or updates it
- update docs so the frontend artifact and deployment path have a single source of truth

If something does depend on it:
- document that dependency explicitly
- explain why the artifact belongs in this repo
- make the ownership and generation path consistent with the rest of the deployment architecture

## Definition of done
There is one documented, authoritative frontend artifact path and `worker/public` is either removed or justified.
